objects.key_discriminator: In Understanding AI and Data, The key shift is from passive awareness to deliberate experimentation with reflection on what happened and why.

common_false_positives.why_not_sufficient: Interest in AI does not yet show structured experimentation.
Trying many tools without criteria does not amount to meaningful exploration.

minimum_threshold_evidence: Runs a purposeful comparison or trial using explicit criteria.
Can describe what changed after exploring more than one option or approach.
strong_threshold_evidence: Keeps notes or evidence from exploration that inform later practice.
Connects observed results to task requirements rather than general preference.
objects.decision_rule: Assign the lower level when evidence is inconsistent, dependent on support, or confined to unusually favourable cases.

objects.key_discriminator: In Understanding AI and Data, The key shift is from trying AI in episodes to integrating it in a dependable, repeatable way.

common_false_positives.why_not_sufficient: A successful experiment may not yet survive normal workload, constraints, or quality requirements.
Repeating the same action is not enough if the reasoning and checks remain weak.

minimum_threshold_evidence: Uses a repeatable workflow in authentic work or study.
Builds in quality checks, review steps, or context-specific constraints.
strong_threshold_evidence: Applies the workflow across multiple cases with stable quality.
Can improve the workflow rather than just executing it.
objects.decision_rule: Assign the lower level when evidence is inconsistent, dependent on support, or confined to unusually favourable cases.

objects.key_discriminator: In Understanding AI and Data, The key shift is from competent personal practice to creating exemplars, standards, or models that shape others' work.

common_false_positives.why_not_sufficient: Doing a lot of AI-supported work does not by itself amount to mastery.
A strong individual method may still be too narrow to guide others or shape quality standards.

minimum_threshold_evidence: Produces exemplars, guidance, or design choices that others can adopt.
Explains why a particular approach fits the field, task, or audience.
strong_threshold_evidence: Mentors others or helps set standards for quality and responsible use.
Reworks practice in response to changing tools, evidence, or field expectations.
objects.decision_rule: Assign the lower level when evidence is inconsistent, dependent on support, or confined to unusually favourable cases.
